formulas.formula: Make your aid, paychecks and family help last the whole semester, and know what you can spend each week.
1. Setup: your school year, term dates (Fall, Spring, Summer), graduation date and how much money you have at the start.
2. Semester Plan: money coming in each term (aid refund, job, family) and big costs going out (fees, books, housing).
3. Monthly Budget: what you can spend each month on food, fun and the rest, plus your monthly bills (rent, phone).
4. Transactions: log money in and money out. Pick a category; money-in categories count as income.
5. Dashboard: your balance, and how much is SAFE TO SPEND each week until the term ends (after the bills still due).
6. Student Loans: what you've borrowed, interest that builds while you're in school, and your estimated payment after graduation.
Balance now minus bills still due this term, divided by the weeks left. Spend less than this and you'll make it.
The money left after aid pays tuition. It usually has to last the whole term.
Use 1 to 28 for bill due days so they work in every month.
Subsidized loans don't build interest while you're in school. Unsubsidized and private loans do.
Loan numbers use simple interest and a 10-year plan. Your servicer's numbers will differ a little.
Clear the white cells on every tab, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: money in, on track, or under budget.
Red: over budget, short, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Good luck this semester.
The basics. Everything else uses these.
Optional: pick a date to preview. Blank = today.
Money in your account at the start
On the first day of the school year.
=IF(R8=0,"Between terms right now.","Now: "&INDEX(B12:B14,R8)&" term, ends "&TEXT(R10,"mmmm d")&".")
Your plan for each term. Living costs = your Monthly Budget x the months in the term (from the term dates on Setup).
Monthly spending money by category. Leave the big term costs (tuition, books, housing, meal plan) blank here: they're on the Semester Plan.
Money in and money out. Money-in categories (aid, scholarship, job, family, other income) add; everything else subtracts.
Your school year month by month. Living = food, fun and everyday spending (not tuition, books, housing or meal plan).
Every student loan. Estimates use simple interest until graduation and a standard 10-year plan.
